title_en: Energy Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated pursuant to the Constitution for the purpose of promoting high-quality energy development, ensuring national energy security, promoting green and low-carbon transformation and sustainable development of the economy and society, actively and steadily advancing the peak of carbon emissions and carbon neutrality, and meeting the needs of comprehensively building a modern socialist country.

Article 2 For the purposes of this Law, 'energy' means various resources that directly or through processing or conversion obtain useful energy, including coal, petroleum, natural gas, nuclear energy, hydropower, wind energy, solar energy, biomass energy, geothermal energy, ocean energy, as well as electricity, heat, hydrogen, and the like.

Article 3 Energy work shall adhere to the leadership of the Communist Party of China, implement the new development philosophy and the holistic approach to national security, coordinate development and security, implement a new energy security strategy that promotes energy consumption revolution, energy supply revolution, energy technology revolution, energy system revolution and comprehensively strengthens international cooperation, adhere to the principles of being based on domestic resources, diversified guarantees, conservation priority, and green development, and accelerate the construction of a new energy system that is clean, low-carbon, safe and efficient.

Article 4 The State shall adhere to the principles of taking multiple measures simultaneously, implementing targeted policies, scientific management, and social co-governance, improve energy conservation policies, strengthen energy conservation management, comprehensively adopt economic, technical, publicity and education measures, and promote comprehensive reduction of energy consumption in all processes and fields of economic and social development, and prevent energy waste.

Article 5 The State shall improve energy development and utilization policies, optimize energy supply structure and consumption structure, actively promote clean and low-carbon energy development, and improve energy utilization efficiency.
The State shall establish a new mechanism for comprehensively shifting from dual control over total energy consumption and intensity to dual control over total carbon emissions and carbon intensity, and accelerate the construction of a dual control system over total carbon emissions and carbon intensity.

Article 6 The State shall accelerate the establishment of an energy market system with diversified entities, unified and open, orderly competition, and effective regulation, regulate energy market order according to law, and equally protect the lawful rights and interests of all types of entities in the energy market.

Article 7 The State shall improve the energy production, supply, storage and sales system, perfect the energy reserve system and energy emergency mechanism, enhance energy supply capacity, and ensure safe, stable, reliable and effective energy supply.

Article 8 The State shall establish and improve an energy standard system to ensure energy security and green and low-carbon transformation, and promote the development of new energy technologies, new industries and new business forms.

Article 9 The State shall strengthen the construction of energy technology innovation capability, support scientific and technological research, application demonstration and industrialization development of energy development and utilization, and provide scientific and technological support for high-quality energy development.
Article 10 The State shall adhere to the principle of equality and mutual benefit, win-win cooperation, and actively promote international energy cooperation.

Article 11 People's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen organizational leadership and overall coordination of energy work, and timely study and resolve major issues in energy work.
People's governments at or above the county level shall incorporate energy work into national economic and social development plans and annual plans.

Article 12 The energy authority of the State Council shall be responsible for national energy work. Other relevant departments of the State Council shall be responsible for related energy work within their respective functions.
The energy authorities of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for energy work within their administrative regions. Other relevant departments of local people's governments at or above the county level shall be responsible for related energy work within their administrative regions within their respective functions.

Article 13 People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall adopt various forms to strengthen publicity and education on energy conservation, energy security and green and low-carbon energy development, enhance the whole society's awareness of energy conservation and energy security, and promote the formation of green and low-carbon production and lifestyle.
News media shall carry out public interest publicity on energy conservation, energy security and green and low-carbon energy development.
Article 14 Entities and individuals that make outstanding contributions in energy work shall be commended and rewarded in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.

Article 15 The State shall formulate and improve energy plans, and give full play to the leading, guiding and regulating role of energy plans for energy development.
Energy plans include comprehensive national energy plan, national energy plans by sector, regional energy plans, and energy plans of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government.

Article 16 The comprehensive national energy plan shall be prepared by the energy authority of the State Council jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council. The comprehensive national energy plan shall be formulated in accordance with the national economic and social development plan and shall be coordinated with relevant plans such as the territorial space plan.
The national energy plan by sector shall be prepared by the energy authority of the State Council jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council in accordance with the comprehensive national energy plan.
The energy authority of the State Council, together with other relevant departments of the State Council and the people's governments of relevant provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government, may prepare a cross-provincial, autonomous region and municipal regional energy plan based on the needs of regional economic and social development, the endowment of energy resources, the characteristics of energy production and consumption, and the requirements of ecological and environmental protection. The regional energy plan shall conform to the comprehensive national energy plan and shall be coordinated with relevant national energy plans by sector.

Article 17 The energy authority of the people's government of a province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government shall, jointly with relevant departments, organize the preparation of the energy plan of that province, autonomous region or municipality in accordance with the comprehensive national energy plan, relevant national energy plans by sector, and relevant regional energy plans.
If the people's government of a city divided into districts or a county needs to prepare an energy plan, it shall be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of the people's government of the province, autonomous region or municipality directly under the Central Government.

Article 18 In preparing an energy plan, the law of energy development shall be followed, overall consideration shall be adhered to, and scientific justification shall be strengthened. The department organizing the preparation of the energy plan shall solicit opinions from relevant departments, relevant enterprises and industry organizations, and relevant experts.
The energy plan shall specify the objectives, main tasks, regional layout, key projects, and safeguard measures for energy development during the planning period.

Article 19 The energy plan shall be implemented after being submitted for approval in accordance with the prescribed authority and procedures.
The approved energy plan shall be published in accordance with the provisions.

Article 20 The department organizing the preparation of the energy plan shall organize and carry out evaluation on the implementation of the energy plan. If adjustment of the energy plan is truly necessary based on the evaluation results, it shall be reported to the original approving authority for consent, unless otherwise provided by the State.

Article 21 The State shall, based on the endowment of energy resources and the needs of sustainable economic and social development, take into overall consideration factors including ensuring energy security, optimizing energy structure, promoting energy transformation and energy conservation, and protecting the ecological environment, and formulate and improve energy development and utilization policies by category.

Article 22 The State shall support the priority development and utilization of renewable energy, rationally develop and cleanly and efficiently utilize fossil energy, promote safe, reliable and orderly substitution of fossil energy by non-fossil energy, and increase the proportion of non-fossil energy consumption.
The energy authority of the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council, formulate medium and long-term development targets for the development and utilization of non-fossil energy, monitor the development and utilization of non-fossil energy on an annual basis, and publish the results to the public.

Article 23 The energy authority of the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council, formulate and organize the implementation of the minimum proportion target of renewable energy in energy consumption.
The State shall improve the guarantee mechanism for the consumption of renewable energy electricity. Power supply enterprises, electricity sales enterprises, relevant electricity users, and enterprises using self-owned power plants for power supply shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, bear the responsibility of consuming renewable energy electricity.
The energy authority of the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council, monitor and assess the implementation of the minimum proportion target of renewable energy in energy consumption and the responsibility of renewable energy electricity consumption.

Article 24 The State shall coordinate hydropower development and ecological protection, and strictly control the development and construction of small hydropower stations.
The development, construction and renovation of hydropower stations shall comply with relevant basin plans, and take into overall consideration the needs of flood control, ecology, water supply, irrigation, navigation, etc.

Article 25 The State shall promote the development and utilization of wind energy and solar energy, adhere to both centralized and distributed approaches, accelerate the construction of wind power and photovoltaic power bases, support the nearby development and utilization of distributed wind power and photovoltaic power, rationally and orderly develop offshore wind power, and actively develop solar thermal power generation.

Article 26 The State shall encourage the rational development and utilization of biomass energy, develop biomass power generation, clean heating using biomass energy, bio-liquid fuels and bio-natural gas according to local conditions.
The State shall promote the large-scale development and utilization of ocean energy, and develop geothermal energy according to local conditions.

Article 27 The State shall actively, safely and orderly develop nuclear power.
The energy authority of the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council, coordinate the national development and layout of nuclear power, and strengthen the management and supervision of nuclear power plant planning, site selection, design, construction, operation and other aspects in accordance with their functions.

Article 28 The State shall optimize the layout of coal development and industrial structure, encourage the development of circular economy in coal mining areas, optimize the coal consumption structure, promote clean and efficient utilization of coal, and give play to the basic guarantee and systematic regulation role of coal in the energy supply system.

Article 29 The State shall take multiple measures to increase the exploration and development of petroleum and natural gas resources, and enhance the domestic supply guarantee capacity of petroleum and natural gas.
Petroleum and natural gas development shall adhere to equal emphasis on onshore and offshore, and encourage large-scale development of unconventional oil and gas resources such as tight oil and gas, shale oil, shale gas, and coalbed methane.
The State shall optimize the layout and structure of petroleum processing and conversion industries, and encourage the adoption of advanced and intensive processing and conversion methods.
The State shall support the rational development and utilization of new types of fuels and industrial raw materials that can replace petroleum and natural gas.

Article 30 The State shall promote the clean and efficient development of coal-fired power generation, rationally layout the construction of coal-fired power plants based on the needs of stable operation of the power system and power supply guarantee, and improve the regulation capacity of coal-fired power generation.

Article 31 The State shall accelerate the construction of a new type of power system, strengthen the coordinated construction of power sources and grids, promote the intelligent transformation of grid infrastructure and the construction of smart microgrids, and improve the grid's capacity to accept, configure and regulate renewable energy.

Article 32 The State shall rationally layout, actively and orderly develop and construct pumped storage power stations, promote the high-quality development of new types of energy storage, and give play to the regulating role of various types of energy storage in the power system.
Article 33 The State shall actively and orderly promote the development and utilization of hydrogen energy, and promote the high-quality development of the hydrogen energy industry.

Article 34 The State shall promote the improvement of energy utilization efficiency, encourage the development of distributed energy and comprehensive energy services with multi-energy complementarity and multi-energy co-supply, actively promote market-based energy conservation services such as contract energy management, and improve the level of cleanness, low-carbon, efficiency and intelligence of terminal energy consumption.
The State shall establish a green energy consumption promotion mechanism through implementing systems such as renewable energy green electricity certificates, and encourage energy users to give priority to the use of clean and low-carbon energy such as renewable energy.
Public institutions shall give priority to the procurement and use of clean and low-carbon energy such as renewable energy, and energy conservation products and services.

Article 35 Energy enterprises and energy users shall equip and use energy and carbon emission measuring instruments in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
Energy users shall reasonably use energy in accordance with safety specifications and relevant provisions on energy conservation, perform the obligation of energy conservation according to law, actively participate in energy demand response, expand green energy consumption, and consciously practice green and low-carbon production and lifestyle.
The State shall strengthen energy demand side management, guide energy users to reasonably adjust their energy use methods, time, quantity, etc., through improving systems such as tiered pricing and time-of-use pricing, so as to promote energy conservation and improve energy utilization efficiency.

Article 36 Enterprises that undertake the supply of energy such as electricity, gas, and heat shall, in accordance with laws, regulations and the relevant provisions of the State, ensure that energy users within their business areas obtain safe, continuous and reliable energy supply services, and shall not refuse or interrupt energy supply services without statutory or agreed reasons, and shall not arbitrarily raise prices, illegally collect fees, reduce supply quantity or restrict purchase quantity.
The enterprises specified in the preceding paragraph shall publicize service standards, charging standards, complaint channels, etc., and provide public inquiry services for energy users.

Article 37 The State shall strengthen the construction and protection of energy infrastructure. No unit or individual shall engage in activities that endanger the safety of energy infrastructure.
The energy authority of the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council, coordinate the construction of cross-provincial, autonomous region and municipal energy infrastructure such as petroleum, natural gas and electricity transmission pipeline networks; the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, in accordance with the energy plan, reserve land and sea for energy infrastructure construction and incorporate them into the territorial space plan.
Energy transmission pipeline network facility operators such as those for petroleum, natural gas and electricity shall improve the operational safety level of energy transmission pipeline networks and ensure the safe operation of energy transmission pipeline network systems. Facilities, equipment and products connected to the energy transmission pipeline network shall meet the requirements for the safe operation of the pipeline network system.

Article 38 The State shall, in accordance with the principles of urban-rural integration, local conditions, multi-energy complementarity, comprehensive utilization, and service improvement, encourage and support the development of energy in rural areas, with priority given to supporting the energy development of rural areas in old revolutionary base areas, ethnic areas, border areas, and underdeveloped areas, and improve the energy supply capacity and service level in rural areas.
Local people's governments at or above the county level shall coordinate the construction of urban and rural energy infrastructure and public service systems, and promote the interconnection of urban and rural energy infrastructure.
When temporary energy supply shortages occur in rural areas, the relevant local people's governments shall take measures to give priority to ensuring energy for rural living and agricultural production.

Article 39 Those engaged in energy development and utilization activities shall comply with the provisions of laws and regulations on ecological and environmental protection, production safety, and occupational disease prevention, reduce pollutant and greenhouse gas emissions, prevent damage to the ecological environment, and prevent and reduce production safety accidents and occupational disease hazards.

Article 40 The State shall encourage and guide all types of business entities to invest in energy development and utilization, energy infrastructure construction, etc., according to law, and promote the development of the energy market.

Article 41 The State shall promote the independent operation of natural monopoly segments and market-oriented reform of competitive segments in the energy sector, strengthen supervision and regulation of natural monopoly businesses in the energy sector according to law, and support all types of business entities to fairly participate in competitive businesses in the energy sector in accordance with market rules according to law.

Article 42 The energy authority of the State Council shall, jointly with other relevant departments of the State Council, coordinate and promote the construction of a unified national energy trading market for coal, electricity, petroleum, natural gas, etc., promote the establishment of market trading institutions or trading platforms with complete functions and standardized operations, expand the scope of trading methods and trading products according to law, and improve trading mechanisms and trading rules.

Article 43 People's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall strengthen coordination, scheduling and organization to ensure smooth energy transportation.
Energy transmission pipeline network facility operators shall improve the fair access and use mechanism, disclose information on access and transmission capacity and operation of energy transmission pipeline network facilities in accordance with provisions, and openly and non-discriminatorily provide energy transmission services to eligible enterprises and other business entities.

Article 44 The State shall encourage upstream and downstream enterprises in the energy sector to strengthen cooperation and coordinated development through methods such as concluding long-term agreements in accordance with laws and market-based approaches, and enhance the ability to respond to energy market risks.
The State shall synergistically promote high-quality development of energy resource exploration, design and construction, equipment manufacturing, project financing, distribution and trade, information services, etc., and enhance the full chain service support capability of upstream and downstream in the energy sector.

Article 45 The State shall promote the establishment of an energy price formation mechanism that is compatible with the socialist market economy system and determined mainly by factors such as energy resource conditions, product and service costs, market supply and demand conditions, and sustainable development conditions.
For energy prices subject to government pricing or government-guided pricing according to law, the pricing authority and specific scope of application shall be based on the central and local pricing catalogs. The formulation and adjustment of energy prices subject to government pricing or government-guided pricing shall comply with the Price Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws, administrative regulations and relevant provisions of the State. Energy enterprises shall provide timely, true and accurate data such as price costs in accordance with the provisions.
The State shall improve the energy price regulation and control system, enhance the effectiveness of energy price regulation, and establish a mechanism to prevent and respond to abnormal fluctuations in energy market prices.
Article 46 The State shall actively promote international investment and trade cooperation in the energy sector, and effectively prevent and respond to risks in the international energy market.

Article 47 The State shall, in accordance with the principles of government leadership, social co-construction, and diversified complementarity, establish and improve an efficient and coordinated energy reserve system, scientifically and reasonably determine the types, scale and methods of energy reserves, and give play to the functions of energy reserves such as strategic guarantee, macro-control and response to urgent needs.

Article 48 Energy reserves shall combine government reserves and enterprise reserves, and coordinate physical reserves, production capacity reserves and mineral reserves.
Government reserves include central government reserves and local government reserves; enterprise reserves include corporate social responsibility reserves and other production and operation inventories of enterprises.
The collection, rotation and use of energy reserves shall be carried out in accordance with laws, administrative regulations and relevant provisions of the State.
The State shall improve the market regulation mechanism of government reserves and take effective measures to respond to risks such as significant market fluctuations.

Article 49 Government reserve storage and operation institutions shall, in accordance with laws, administrative regulations and relevant provisions of the State, establish and improve internal management systems, strengthen reserve management, and ensure the safety of government reserves.
Corporate social responsibility reserves shall be established on the principle of enterprise ownership, policy guidance, and effective supervision. Energy enterprises undertaking social responsibility reserves shall fulfill their reserve obligations in accordance with the prescribed types and quantities, and accept supervision and management from relevant government departments.
Specific measures for energy production capacity reserves shall be formulated by the energy authority of the State Council jointly with the finance department of the State Council and other relevant departments.
Specific measures for energy mineral reserves shall be formulated by the natural resources authority of the State Council jointly with the energy authority of the State Council, the finance department of the State Council and other relevant departments.

Article 50 The State shall improve the energy reserve supervision system, accelerate the construction of energy reserve facilities, improve the professional level of energy reserve operation entities, strengthen the informatization construction of energy reserves, and continuously enhance the comprehensive effectiveness of energy reserves.

The State shall establish and improve the energy forecasting and early warning system, enhance the capability and level of energy forecasting and early warning, and conduct timely and effective forecasting and early warning of changes in energy supply and demand, fluctuations in energy prices, and the status of energy security risks.
Energy forecasting and early warning information shall be released by the energy administration department of the State Council.

The State shall establish an energy emergency management system featuring unified leadership, hierarchical responsibility, and coordinated linkage.
People's governments at or above the county level shall take effective measures to strengthen the energy emergency response system, regularly conduct energy emergency drills and training, and improve energy emergency response capabilities.

The energy administration department of the State Council shall, in conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council, draft the national energy emergency response plan, which shall be implemented upon approval by the State Council.
The energy administration department of the State Council shall, in conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council, strengthen guidance and coordination of cross-provincial, cross-autonomous region, and cross-municipality energy emergency work.
People's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, based on the actual conditions of their respective administrative regions, formulate energy emergency response plans for their administrative regions.
The formulation of energy emergency response plans by the people's governments of cities divided into districts and county-level people's governments shall be decided by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government.
Relatively large energy enterprises and energy-consuming entities shall, in accordance with state regulations, formulate their own energy emergency response plans.

When the energy emergency situation specified in Article 54 of this Law occurs, energy enterprises, energy users, and other relevant entities and individuals shall obey the unified command and arrangements of the relevant people's government, assume corresponding energy emergency obligations in accordance with regulations, cooperate in taking emergency response measures, and assist in maintaining the order of the energy market.
If losses are caused to relevant entities or individuals due to the implementation of energy emergency response measures, the relevant people's government shall compensate them according to law.

The State shall formulate policies and measures to encourage and support energy technology innovation, and promote the establishment of an energy technology innovation system that is led by national strategic scientific and technological forces, with enterprises as the mainstay, market-oriented, and deeply integrated with industry, academia, and research.

The State shall encourage and support the research, development, demonstration, promotion, application, and industrial development of fundamental, key, and cutting-edge major technologies, equipment, and related new materials in the fields of energy resource exploration and development, clean and efficient utilization of fossil energy, development and utilization of renewable energy, safe utilization of nuclear energy, development and utilization of hydrogen energy, as well as energy storage and energy conservation.
Energy technology innovation shall be included in the key support areas of relevant national plans for scientific and technological development and high-tech industry development.
The State shall formulate and improve policies on industry, finance, government procurement, etc., to encourage and guide social funds to invest in energy technology innovation.

The State shall establish major energy technology innovation platforms, support the construction of major energy science and technology infrastructure and public service platforms for energy technology research and development, testing, inspection, certification, etc., and enhance the capability of energy technology innovation and service.

The State shall support the centralized conduct of scientific and technological research and integrated application demonstration based on major energy projects, and promote collaborative innovation among industry, academia, and research as well as the upstream and downstream industrial and supply chains of energy.

The State shall support the application of advanced information technology in the energy sector, promote the digital and intelligent development of energy production and supply, as well as the collaborative conversion and integrated complementarity of multiple energy sources.

The State shall intensify the training of professional talents in energy science and technology, and encourage and support educational institutions, scientific research institutions, and enterprises to cooperate in cultivating high-quality professional talents in energy science and technology.

The energy administration department and other relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall, in accordance with their respective functions and duties, strengthen supervision and inspection of relevant energy work, and promptly investigate and deal with illegal acts.

The energy administration department and other relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level shall strengthen coordination in energy regulation, enhance regulatory efficiency, and may establish energy regulatory information systems as needed for work.
Relevant entities shall, in accordance with regulations, submit relevant information to the energy administration department and other relevant departments.

The energy administration department of the State Council shall, in conjunction with the relevant departments of the State Council, strengthen the construction of the credit system in the energy industry, and establish a credit recording system in accordance with relevant state regulations.

Disputes arising from the access to and use of energy transmission pipeline network facilities may be mediated by the energy administration department of the people's government at or above the provincial level; if mediation fails, the parties may institute prosecution in the People's Court; the parties may also directly institute prosecution in the People's Court.

Any entity or individual shall have the right to report to the energy administration department or other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level any act that violates this Law and other laws and regulations related to energy. The department receiving the report shall handle it promptly according to law.

Any staff member of the energy administration department or other relevant departments of a people's government at or above the county level who violates the provisions of this Law by abusing power, neglecting duty, or engaging in malpractice for personal gain shall be given sanctions according to law.

If an enterprise responsible for the supply of energy such as electricity, gas, and heat, in violation of this Law, refuses or interrupts energy supply services to energy users within its business area without statutory or contractual grounds, or arbitrarily raises prices, illegally charges fees, reduces the quantity of supply, or restricts the quantity of purchase, the energy administration department or other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall order correction and impose administrative penalties according to law; if the circumstances are serious, the relevant persons in charge and directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

If an enterprise operating energy transmission pipeline network facilities, in violation of this Law, fails to open and provide energy transmission services to qualified enterprises and other business entities in a fair and non-discriminatory manner, the energy administration department or other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the provincial level shall order correction and give a warning or a notice of criticism; if it refuses to correct, it shall be fined not more than two times the amount of economic losses suffered by the relevant business entities; if the circumstances are serious, the relevant persons in charge and directly responsible persons shall be given sanctions according to law.

If, in violation of this Law, an energy enterprise, an energy user, or any other relevant entity or individual, during an energy emergency situation, fails to obey the unified command and arrangements of the relevant people's government, fails to assume energy emergency obligations in accordance with regulations, or fails to cooperate with the adoption of emergency response measures, the energy administration department or other relevant departments of the people's government at or above the county level shall order correction and give a warning or a notice of criticism; if it refuses to correct, a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 50,000 yuan shall be imposed on the individual, and a fine of not less than 100,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan shall be imposed on the entity, and depending on the severity of the circumstances, the entity may be ordered to suspend business for rectification or its relevant permits may be revoked according to law.

Whoever, in violation of this Law, causes property loss or other damage shall bear civil liability according to law; if the act constitutes a violation of public security administration, public security administration penalties shall be imposed according to law; if a crime is constituted, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.

For the purposes of this Law, the following terms have the meanings set forth below:
(1) "Fossil energy" means energy evolved from ancient animal and plant fossils through geological processes, including coal, petroleum, natural gas, etc.
(2) "Renewable energy" means energy that can be continuously supplemented and regenerated through natural processes in a relatively short period, including hydropower, wind energy, solar energy, biomass energy, geothermal energy, ocean energy, etc.
(3) "Non-fossil energy" means energy obtained without reliance on fossil fuels, including renewable energy and nuclear energy.
(4) "Biomass energy" means energy converted from plants in nature and urban and rural organic waste through biological, chemical, or physical processes.
(5) "Hydrogen energy" means energy released through chemical reactions where hydrogen serves as an energy carrier.

The management of energy development and utilization by the armed forces shall be implemented in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State and the armed forces.
If the State has other provisions on the development and utilization of nuclear energy, those provisions shall apply.

If an international treaty on energy concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China contains provisions different from those of this Law, the provisions of the international treaty shall apply, except for the clauses on which the People's Republic of China has declared reservations.

If any country or region adopts discriminatory prohibitions, restrictions, or other similar measures against the People's Republic of China in the renewable energy industry or other energy fields, the People's Republic of China may adopt corresponding measures against that country or region based on the actual circumstances.

If any organization or individual outside the territory of the People's Republic of China commits acts that endanger the national energy security of the People's Republic of China, legal liability shall be investigated according to law.
This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2025.
